scope: Read-only independent review of frozen integrated CYD output-backend telemetry, pinned SDK driver callback/IRAM contracts, health serialization/HTTP forwarding and host evidence. No production/test/Git edits, SDK/app builds, rerun of test suites or device access.
limits: No production/test/Git changes, SDK/app build, test-suite rerun or device operation occurred in this independent review.
Empty actionable findings are not hardware approval; existing target helper review and current host evidence are retained with their explicit scope limits.

reviewed_contracts.subject: PDM callback lifetime and order
reviewed_contracts.conclusion: Callback is registered after successful PDM mode initialization and before any preload/enable. Registration failure takes the existing release(false) cleanup and propagates its original error. The SDK copies the stack-local callback descriptor while READY; user_data is NULL. Callback ignores channel/event/context and touches only boot-lifetime metrics state, so it retains no descriptor, event or destroyed channel pointer. Queue availability is explicitly boot-cumulative, including successful registration before a later startup failure.

reviewed_contracts.subject: Pinned classic ESP32 I2S API and queue semantics
reviewed_contracts.conclusion: SDK6.0.2 i2s_common.h documents ISR callbacks and READY/REGISTERED registration; i2s_common.c copies callbacks and validates IRAM/internal context when configured. Its classic interrupt path invokes on_send_q_ovf after removing a full completion-queue entry and ORs the returned wake flag. Returning false does not erase other SDK wake requests. This is a lost completion-queue event, not evidence of an audible underrun. Existing disable/stop and channel deletion remove the source through SDK ownership; no new callback context requires explicit deregistration.

reviewed_contracts.subject: IRAM and lock structure
reviewed_contracts.conclusion: New PDM wrapper is IRAM_ATTR and calls only the previously audited IRAM queue-drop helper. Static state and lock are DRAM_ATTR; the helper uses ISR critical entry/exit and no allocator, log or timer API. Task begin/end/snapshot never hold metrics lock across driver calls or clock reads. Prior helper target-object review remains applicable because helper source hashes match exactly. Final linked integrated callback/helper placement and hardware IRQ timing are not established by these host tests.

reviewed_contracts.subject: All three backend write accounting
reviewed_contracts.conclusion: PDM, continuous DAC and legacy adapter hooks surround their synchronous write APIs, preserve every original return and incomplete-write check, and pass requested/reported bytes in the API caller buffer units. Every DAC written pointer is initialized by its caller. Legacy passes frames*sizeof(uint32_t), not frame or input-PCM count. Prime/bias/idle writes through these APIs are included; PDM preload_data is deliberately excluded and documented separately. Paused paths that return before the driver create no observation.

reviewed_contracts.subject: Snapshot and health publication
reviewed_contracts.conclusion: The handler obtains one coherent metrics snapshot by value and forwards all fields to the runtime struct. JSON uses exact PRIu32/PRIu64 widths, preserves saturation and timing counters, emits null for unavailable queue/time observations and numeric zero after a valid zero observation. It never reports zero as measured when no timer sample exists. New groups stay below the 256-byte formatting chunk and existing 2304-byte response capacity. Worst-width integration evidence is 2000 bytes and capacity canaries cover all boundaries.

reviewed_contracts.subject: Evidence attribution
reviewed_contracts.conclusion: Byte-exact complete output and metrics TUs are compiled as separate host units in all three backends and quiet/diagnostic modes. Metrics16/7 and backend22/8 raw positive and named semantic mutant logs match reports. Health three profiles and maximum JSON/null/zero markers match raw logs. Stream handler forwards every supplied driver field and retains50 stream/80 settings cases. Their scopes correctly identify SDK/platform/release/snapshot seams; no backend or physical qualification is inferred from serializer/HTTP-only tests.

uncovered_or_seamed_paths: Backend fixture replaces SDK driver operations, IRAM/DRAM attributes, GPIO, clock and ISR/portMUX behavior with explicit host seams. Its pthread concurrency test does not simulate ESP32 interrupt masking, actual SDK queue scheduling or prove interrupt-latency/performance bounds.

PDM cleanup after registration failure is exercised with successful channel deletion. Delete/disable failure-and-retry and preload/enable failure combinations are not exhaustively injected by this new telemetry suite. Source review found no new changed ownership branch defect; most surrounding cleanup/retry code predates telemetry.

The PDM callback registration struct and event types in host platform.h are models. Actual pinned SDK declaration/implementation compatibility was reviewed directly; parent firmware/target compile remains the gate for integrated compiler/linker ABI and final wrapper/helper IRAM placement.

Health tests supply synthetic driver snapshots to the serializer; stream tests supply a snapshot seam to the real handler. They complement complete-backend tests and do not independently exercise driver allocation, callback registration or DMA.

No TSAN, physical board playback, DMA-transmitted byte count, audible underrun rate, resource-margin, heap-saving or throughput claim is established. Requested/reported buffer bytes, completion queue drops and whole API wall time retain their documented narrower meanings.
